title: Baseline characterization and live-gap reconciliation
desired_outcome: Establish a trusted baseline from the live repository, add the minimum characterization coverage needed for safe refactoring, and prove the bundle is execution-ready before architectural mutation work begins.
acceptance: Prepared-stage validator passes.
The risky current behaviors are mapped to explicit tests or an explicit uncovered-gap list.
The execution report clearly states what proof exists and what still needs to be added in later phases.
No production behavior has been changed beyond baseline/testability scaffolding.
tests_to_add_or_update: Focused test run proving the selected characterization tests pass.
risk_notes: If the baseline is weak or the prepared-stage validator fails, repair the bundle or add characterization tests first. No canonical refactor may begin until this phase passes. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Canonical dependency model and compatibility boundary
desired_outcome: Replace the current dual dependency meaning with one canonical dependency model and quarantine any legacy compatibility behavior behind a single explicit boundary.
acceptance: Core code uses one canonical dependency representation.
Any remaining legacy dependency handling is isolated behind one compatibility boundary.
Runtime, read, and persistence logic no longer each reconstruct dependency meaning differently.
Regression tests prove canonical round-trip behavior.
tests_to_add_or_update: Focused integration tests around save/load/publish/clone/runtime dependency behavior.
Any needed component tests proving canvas/workspace surfaces still reflect the canonical dependency graph.
risk_notes: If canonicality is still ambiguous, stop and use the foundation corrective playbook before any validation/persistence work continues. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Side-effect-free validation and editor-normalization split
desired_outcome: Make validation pure and move normalization into explicit, intentionally named entry points so correctness checks no longer mutate the thing being validated.
acceptance: Validation methods no longer mutate state.
Normalization is called explicitly at clear entry points.
Tests prove validation purity and normalization idempotence.
No hidden dependency-sync side effects remain in validation.
tests_to_add_or_update: Regression tests for save and editor flows proving behavior still works after the split.
risk_notes: If validation still mutates state or normalization remains hidden, trigger the foundation corrective playbook and do not continue into transaction or persistence work. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Architecture review gate A
desired_outcome: Stop after the baseline, canonical dependency, and validation-purity work, then perform a strict architectural review before any transaction or persistence refactor begins.
acceptance: A written gate memo exists.
The gate decision is explicit.
If failed, a corrective subbundle is created and downstream work is blocked.
risk_notes: Create a gate-A corrective subbundle from `subbundles/_corrective-foundation-stabilization` or `subbundles/_corrective-template`, block the queue, and rerun gate A after the correction lands. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Transaction, concurrency, and conflict hardening
desired_outcome: Add explicit transaction boundaries, provider-agnostic optimistic concurrency, and clean conflict translation for the critical Process mutation flows.
acceptance: Critical process aggregates use provider-agnostic optimistic concurrency.
Save/publish/transition flows are wrapped in explicit transactions.
Conflict failures return explicit domain/result meaning instead of raw exceptions.
Multi-context conflict tests exist and pass.
tests_to_add_or_update: Integration tests proving conflict handling and rollback behavior.
risk_notes: If conflict behavior is still ambiguous or provider-specific, trigger the persistence/concurrency corrective playbook before differential persistence begins. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Differential definition-graph persistence
desired_outcome: Replace the current delete-and-recreate definition save behavior with differential graph persistence so stable logical children retain identity and saves become less destructive.
acceptance: No-op save preserves child IDs.
Editing one step or role does not recreate unrelated children.
Artifact, assignment, dependency, and branch links remain intact across targeted updates.
Rollback tests show no partial child graph remains after failure.
tests_to_add_or_update: Integration tests proving stable child identity.
risk_notes: If unchanged logical children still churn or rollback proof is weak, trigger the persistence/concurrency corrective playbook before publication work starts. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Architecture review gate B
desired_outcome: Stop after transaction/concurrency hardening and differential persistence, then decide whether the mutation core is now strong enough for publication and runtime decomposition.
acceptance: A written gate-B memo exists.
The mutation-core decision is explicit.
Any failing outcome created a corrective subbundle and blocked the queue.
risk_notes: Create a gate-B corrective subbundle from `subbundles/_corrective-persistence-and-concurrency-reset` or `subbundles/_corrective-template`, block the queue, and rerun gate B after the correction lands. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Publication, versioning, and clone-engine decomposition
desired_outcome: Separate publication lifecycle concerns from graph cloning, harden version/slug conflict handling, and remove publication-era dependence on legacy compatibility paths.
acceptance: Publication lifecycle and clone logic are responsibility-separated.
Version and slug conflict handling is explicit and race-aware.
Publish/draft creation still preserves canonical dependency behavior.
Delete behavior remains correct after the split.
tests_to_add_or_update: Integration tests for publish, delete, and clone behavior.
risk_notes: If publication remains coupled or conflict-prone, trigger the runtime/query corrective playbook before runtime extraction begins. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Runtime state-machine and transition-policy extraction
desired_outcome: Extract the runtime transition hotspot into smaller policy and planning services so runtime behavior becomes easier to test, review, and maintain without changing the public command surface.
acceptance: The main runtime orchestration method is materially smaller or thinner.
Extracted policy/planner responsibilities are explicit and testable.
Selected branch routing and non-selected path handling still behave deterministically.
Existing runtime callers remain compatible.
tests_to_add_or_update: Integration tests for runtime transition behavior.
Any new unit tests for extracted policy/planner services.
risk_notes: If runtime logic is still effectively centralized or weakly proven, trigger the runtime/query corrective playbook before read-side work continues. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Read-side query splitting and performance hardening
desired_outcome: Split broad query logic into focused projection/query services and reduce unnecessary in-memory aggregation or full-graph loading for common read surfaces.
acceptance: Common read surfaces now have clearer query ownership.
Obvious broad in-memory aggregation patterns are reduced or removed.
Read-side behavior remains correct after the split.
The query layer remains projection-only.
tests_to_add_or_update: Focused integration tests proving query correctness.
risk_notes: If the query split is superficial or still dominated by broad loads, trigger the runtime/query corrective playbook before consolidation and UI work begins. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Architecture review gate C
desired_outcome: Stop after publication, runtime, and read-side work, then decide whether the module is truly moving toward smaller responsibilities and healthier behavior/projection boundaries.
acceptance: A written gate-C memo exists.
The architectural direction of publication/runtime/query work is explicitly judged.
Any fail result blocks downstream work and creates corrective scope.
risk_notes: Create a gate-C corrective subbundle from `subbundles/_corrective-runtime-and-query-reset` or `subbundles/_corrective-template`, block the queue, and rerun gate C after the correction lands. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Template subsystem and cross-module shared-infrastructure consolidation
desired_outcome: Remove the real duplicated helper hotspots in template and adjacent modules without creating a generic dumping ground or blurring domain ownership.
acceptance: The main duplicated helper hotspots are reduced in active code.
Ownership of extracted helpers is clearer, not blurrier.
Role snapshot summary building is defined in one place if the semantics truly match.
Tests prove parity for the extracted helpers.
tests_to_add_or_update: Any additional unit tests for extracted helpers.
risk_notes: If consolidation increases coupling or leaves major duplication active, trigger the workspace/shared-infrastructure corrective playbook before the next phase continues. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Workspace and canvas decomposition
desired_outcome: Break the oversized Process workspace and related canvas orchestration into smaller components and clearer state ownership without pushing domain rules into Razor code.
acceptance: The workspace/canvas surface is materially easier to navigate and reason about.
Extracted components or presenters have coherent ownership.
Existing workspace/canvas behaviors remain covered by tests.
Browser proof shows the UI still reads and behaves coherently on large and narrow viewports.
tests_to_add_or_update: Focused component tests for the extracted workspace/canvas behavior.
Real browser proof on `/processes` with large-screen and narrower-width screenshots.
risk_notes: If the workspace is still effectively monolithic or the UI proof is weak, trigger the workspace/shared-infrastructure corrective playbook before schema cleanup continues. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Schema hygiene, migrations, and long-file split
desired_outcome: Finish the core hardening by improving entity/configuration auditability, synchronizing provider snapshots or migrations, and reducing remaining long-file concentration in the touched process core.
acceptance: Touched model/configuration files are easier to audit.
Relationship/delete behavior is explicit where the initiative changed it.
SQLite and PostgreSQL snapshots or migrations are coherent.
The build remains healthy after the split.
risk_notes: If schema/configuration hygiene is still weak or providers drifted, trigger the workspace/shared-infrastructure corrective playbook before final closure begins. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Architecture review gate D
desired_outcome: Stop after consolidation, workspace decomposition, and schema hygiene to decide whether the module is now architecturally strong enough for final closure proof.
acceptance: A written gate-D memo exists.
The architectural strength of the final cleanup batch is explicitly judged.
Any failing outcome blocks final closure and creates corrective work.
risk_notes: Create a gate-D corrective subbundle from `subbundles/_corrective-workspace-and-shared-infrastructure-reset` or `subbundles/_corrective-template`, block the queue, and rerun gate D after the correction lands. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.

title: Final regression proof and bundle closure
desired_outcome: Run the final proof matrix, capture browser evidence, close the raw user notes against real evidence, and synchronize the whole bundle to the actually shipped state.
acceptance: All required validators, builds, tests, and browser proofs have been run and recorded.
The execution report is fully populated from fresh evidence.
Raw user notes are closed note by note with proof references.
The completed-stage validator passes.
tests_to_add_or_update: Full targeted build/test proof matrix from `09-proof-contract.md`.
Final browser proof on `/processes` where UI changed.
risk_notes: If final proof is missing or any validator fails, keep the bundle open and create a targeted corrective subbundle before closure is attempted again. Do not continue past the progression gate if proof is weak.
